facts.statement: Pamparaptor is an extinct paravian theropod dinosaur known from the Late Cretaceous of Argentine Patagonia.
facts.quote: Pamparaptor (, meaning "thief of the Pampas") is an extinct genus of paravian theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Portezuelo Formation of the Neuquén province in Argentine Patagonia.

facts.statement: The only known species, P. micros, is represented by a single fossilized left foot featuring a distinctive killing claw.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, P. micros (from the Greek word for "small"), which is known from a single specimen consisting of a mostly complete and fully-articulated left foot, which preserves the iconic dromaeosaur-like "killing claw".

facts.statement: The sole specimen was discovered in 2005 by technician Diego Rosales while working for the Lake Barreales Paleontological Center.
facts.quote: The type and only specimen of Pamparaptor was discovered in 2005 by a technician named Diego Rosales who was working for the Lake Barreales Paleontological Center (or CePaLB) at the National University of Comahue.

facts.statement: The fossil was found at the Baal Quarry, an outcrop of the Portezuelo Formation dated to the late Turonian or early Coniacian.
facts.quote: It was found at a locality called the "Baal Quarry", which is an outcrop of the Portezuelo Formation dated to the late Turonian or early Coniacian.

facts.statement: The genus was formally described in 2010 by a team including Juan Porfiri, Jorge Calvo, and Domenica Dos Santos.
facts.quote: Pamparaptor was finally described as a new genus in a publication of the Annals of the Brazilian Academy of Sciences in 2010 by a team of researchers including Juan Porfiri, Jorge Calvo, and Domenica Dos Santos.

facts.statement: Pamparaptor was a small dromaeosaur with a metatarsal measuring approximately 9.3 cm in length.
facts.quote: Pamparaptor was a small dromaeosaur. The entire length of the metatarsal (the longest bone in the foot) is only about 9.3 cm.

facts.statement: Later researchers estimated the animal's length at about 1.15 meters and its weight at 2.6 kilograms.
facts.quote: They did not give an estimate of the animal's mass. Rubén Molina-Pérez and Asier Larramendi gave a slightly greater length estimate of about 1.15 m long and they also gave a weight estimate of 2.6 kg in weight.

facts.statement: While its precise classification remains uncertain, the original authors argued that it belongs to the dromaeosaurid family.
facts.quote: Its precise classification is uncertain, but the authors who described this taxon have argued that it is a dromaeosaurid.

facts.statement: The authors rejected the hypothesis that the related genus Neuquenraptor was a junior synonym of Unenlagia.
facts.quote: They also rejected the earlier conclusion from other researchers that Neuquenraptor was a junior synonym of Unenlagia.

facts.statement: A 2024 study recovered Pamparaptor as an unenlagiine, but also as a sister taxon to anchiornithids, troodontids, and microraptorian dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: In a 2024 study, while the authors considered Pamparaptor as an unenlagiine based on phylogenetic analyses, Pamparaptor was also recovered as a sister taxon to various groups of paravians such as the anchiornithids, troodontids and microraptorian dromaeosaurids.

facts.statement: The Portezuelo Formation, where the fossil was found, was deposited from the late Turonian to the early Coniacian.
facts.quote: The formation as a whole is about 95-130 m thick, and was likely deposited over a period roughly from the late Turonian to the early Coniacian.

facts.statement: The fossil-bearing environment was an alluvial fan composed of mudstones, siltstones, and claystones.
facts.quote: The Portezuelo Formation is primarily composed of yellow and red-brown mudstones and siltstones which alternate with claystones and indicate the region contained an alluvial fan.

facts.statement: Researchers have debated whether Pamparaptor might have affinities with troodontids due to similarities in foot anatomy.
facts.quote: Possible troodontid affinities were also examined for Pamparaptor due to several features of the foot anatomy that resembled troodontids.

facts.statement: The specimen was initially thought to be a juvenile or subadult of the related genus Neuquenraptor because it was much smaller and shared similarities with it.
facts.quote: The specimen bore some similarities to the contemporaneous taxon Neuquenraptor, but was much smaller. For those reasons, MUCPv-1163 was believed to be a juvenile or subadult specimen of Neuquenraptor.

facts.statement: The genus Pamparaptor was named by Juan D. Porfiri, Jorge O. Calvo, and Domenica dos Santos in 2011.
facts.quote: Pamparaptor fue nombrado por Juan D. Porfiri, Jorge O. Calvo y Domenica dos Santos en el año de 2011

facts.statement: The species is known from holotype MUCPv-1163, an articulated and nearly complete left foot.
facts.quote: Es conocido a partir del holotipo MUCPv-1163, un pie izquierdo articulado y casi completo.

facts.statement: Pamparaptor lived during the late Cretaceous, specifically the Turonian and Coniacian stages, approximately 89 million years ago.
facts.quote: vivió a fines del período Cretácico durante el Turoniense y el Coniaciense, hace aproximadamente 89 millones de años

facts.statement: Fossils of Pamparaptor were found in Neuquén Province, Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: fue encontrado en la provincia de Neuquén, en la Patagonia, Argentina

facts.statement: The specimen was recovered from the Portezuelo Formation, part of the Río Neuquén Subgroup of the Neuquén Group.
facts.quote: El ejemplar fue recuperado de la formación de Portezuelo, parte del Subgrupo Río Neuquén del Grupo Neuquén.

facts.statement: Pamparaptor is a basal dromaeosaurid with feet similar to those of troodontids.
facts.quote: Es un dromeosáurido basal con pies similares a los de los troodóntidos

facts.statement: The species name micros means "small" and refers to the specimen's estimated length of 0.5 to 0.7 meters.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, micros, que significa "pequeño", se refiere al tamaño del espécimen, un estimado en unos 0,5 a 0,7 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: The genus authority for Pamparaptor is Porfiri, Calvo & Santos, 2011.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Porfiri, Calvo & Santos, 2011

facts.statement: Pamparaptor belongs to the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Dromaeosauridae

facts.statement: The parent group of Pamparaptor is Deinonychosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Deinonychosauria

facts.statement: The time range for Pamparaptor is from the Turonian to the Coniacian, between 93.9 and 85.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Coniacian (93.9 to 85.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The holotype was first reported in scientific literature in 2007 before being formally described as a new genus in 2011.
rejected.quote: The holotype specimen of Pamparaptor was first reported in the literature in 2007 by the same researchers who would later go on to describe it.
